metadata.title: GYNAECOLOGY & OBSTETRICS OSCE
metadata.subtitle: 15 Structured Stations
metadata.audienceAndScoring: Final-Year MBBS • 8 minutes per station • 20-point analytic checklist
metadata.includedMaterials: Candidate materials • Standardised scripts • Examiner guides • Learning notes
facultyNote: Built in the same architecture as the preceding OSCE manuals. All patient names in source-derived scenarios have been changed.
The uploaded notes are used as the scenario base for menopause, dysmenorrhoea, PCOS/hirsutism, vaginal discharge/STI assessment, infertility, contraception and pre-conception counselling.
The station mix deliberately includes 9 obstetric and 6 gynaecology stations, reflecting the strong obstetric weighting used in CPSP MCPS TOACS while remaining suitable for final-year MBBS practice.

Older statements in the source notes are not copied blindly. Exact drug doses, antihypertensive thresholds, magnesium sulphate regimens, thromboprophylaxis, abortion law/process, contraceptive eligibility and emergency protocols must be checked against current approved institutional, provincial and national guidance before summative use.
Core priorities are respectful communication, consent/chaperone use, maternal stabilisation, fetal assessment, timely escalation, interpretation of common clinical data and safe management planning.
assessmentDesign: Each station uses 10 observable criteria scored 0–2 (20 marks).
Critical safety errors may justify an overall fail despite the analytic score.
Local policy and current national guidance supersede this teaching document.
contents: 15. Early Pregnancy Pain & Bleeding — Suspected Ectopic Pregnancy

stations.title: Menopause — Focused History & Counselling
candidateInstructions: Mrs Nadia Farooq, 49, reports hot flushes, night sweats, vaginal dryness and sleep disturbance.
Take a focused history and explain your assessment and management options. Examination is not required.
candidateHandout: Clarify menstrual pattern and last menstrual period.
Screen for postmenopausal bleeding, mood symptoms, cardiovascular/bone risk and contraindications to systemic hormone therapy.
simulationScript: Last menstrual period 16 months ago; periods became irregular before stopping.
Hot flushes and night sweats disturb sleep. Vaginal dryness and dyspareunia; recurrent urinary symptoms.
No postmenopausal bleeding. Mild hypertension. Smokes 10 cigarettes/day.
Concern: “Will I get osteoporosis or a heart attack now?”
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Likely natural menopause based on age, symptoms and >12 months amenorrhoea; routine FSH testing is usually unnecessary in typical women over 45 unless diagnosis is uncertain.
Discuss lifestyle, smoking cessation, exercise, calcium/vitamin D adequacy and bone/cardiovascular risk assessment.
For bothersome vasomotor symptoms discuss systemic menopausal hormone therapy when appropriate after contraindication/risk review; uterus present requires endometrial protection.
For genitourinary symptoms discuss vaginal moisturisers/lubricants and low-dose vaginal oestrogen when suitable.
Any postmenopausal bleeding requires prompt evaluation.
suggestedApproach: Establish menstrual status → symptom burden → red flags → risk/contraindication review → shared treatment decision → safety net.

checklist.criterion: Introduces self, confirms identity, privacy and consent.
Confirms LMP, amenorrhoea duration and prior cycle change.
Assesses vasomotor, sleep, mood and genitourinary symptoms.
Specifically asks about postmenopausal bleeding.
Reviews VTE, breast/endometrial cancer, liver/cardiovascular history and relevant medications.
Assesses smoking, BP, weight, bone and lifestyle risks.
Explains likely menopause accurately and avoids unnecessary routine FSH testing in a typical >45-year-old.
Discusses non-pharmacological and hormone/non-hormone options using shared decision-making.
Explains vaginal oestrogen/lubricant options for genitourinary symptoms.
Safety-nets bleeding and arranges follow-up/review.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: When is FSH testing useful?
What symptom mandates investigation rather than reassurance?
criticalSafetyErrors: Reassuring postmenopausal bleeding without investigation.
Offering systemic hormone therapy without reviewing contraindications and uterine status.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded menopause scenario; patient name changed. Investigation and treatment wording modernised.

stations.title: Primary Dysmenorrhoea — Focused Adolescent Consultation
candidateInstructions: Ms Areeba Shah, 17, has cramping lower abdominal pain during the first 1–2 days of menstruation and misses college because of it.
Take a focused history and explain initial management.
candidateHandout: Establish whether pain is primary or suggests secondary pathology.
Use age-appropriate confidentiality and sensitive sexual history where relevant.
simulationScript: Menarche at 14; cycles regular every 28–30 days; normal flow.
Pain began about a year after menarche, occurs with onset of bleeding, radiates to back and improves after 1–2 days.
Occasional nausea/diarrhoea. No intermenstrual bleeding, abnormal discharge or chronic pelvic pain.
Not sexually active. Main concern is missing classes.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Pattern is compatible with primary dysmenorrhoea.
No routine pelvic examination or extensive investigation is required when history is classic and there are no red flags.
Management: education, heat/exercise and NSAID therapy if appropriate; hormonal contraception can be considered if desired/suitable.
Refer/investigate for secondary causes if new severe pain, dyspareunia, abnormal bleeding/discharge, infertility, pelvic mass, or failure of adequate first-line treatment.
suggestedApproach: Confidential setting → menstrual/pain history → secondary red flags → impact/ICE → first-line plan → review.

checklist.criterion: Establishes confidentiality and obtains consent.
Characterises timing, severity, radiation and relation to menstruation.
Takes menstrual history including regularity, flow and intermenstrual bleeding.
Screens pregnancy/STI risk sensitively when relevant.
Screens secondary causes: discharge, dyspareunia, chronic pelvic pain, bowel/bladder symptoms.
Assesses impact on school/work and analgesic use.
Recognises likely primary dysmenorrhoea.
Offers appropriate non-pharmacological and NSAID first-line measures.
Discusses hormonal options if appropriate and patient interested.
Provides review and safety-net criteria for investigation/referral.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: Name two features suggesting secondary dysmenorrhoea.
Why may examination be unnecessary in a typical adolescent presentation?
criticalSafetyErrors: Ignoring pregnancy possibility in a sexually active patient.
Failure to investigate progressive/red-flag pelvic pain.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded primary dysmenorrhoea scenario; patient name changed and testing simplified to current clinical reasoning.

stations.title: PCOS / Hirsutism — Assessment & Counselling
stations.primaryCompetency: Endocrine-gynaecology history, differential and long-term risk counselling
candidateInstructions: Ms Hiba Qureshi, 23, presents with increasing facial hair and weight gain.
Take a focused history, propose investigations and counsel her about likely management.
candidateHandout: Assess menstrual dysfunction, hyperandrogenism and metabolic risk.
Exclude important mimics and urgent virilisation.
simulationScript: Facial hair increasing for 8 months; acne present.
Cycles every 45–60 days. BMI 32 kg/m².
No rapid voice deepening, clitoromegaly or severe sudden virilisation.
Concerned about appearance and future fertility.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: PCOS is likely if ovulatory dysfunction and clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism are present after excluding alternative causes.
Assess BP/BMI, pregnancy possibility, androgen excess severity and metabolic risk.

Investigations may include pregnancy test when relevant, total/free androgen assessment, TSH/prolactin and other tests guided by presentation; pelvic ultrasound is not required in every case to make the diagnosis.
Lifestyle/weight management is central. Discuss menstrual protection, acne/hirsutism treatment and fertility planning according to goals; screen for dysglycaemia and other cardiometabolic risk.
suggestedApproach: Symptoms → menstrual history → virilisation red flags → metabolic risk → exclude mimics → goal-based management.

checklist.criterion: Introduces self, obtains consent and explores patient priorities.
Characterises hirsutism/acne onset and progression.
Takes full menstrual and pregnancy/contraception history.
Screens rapid virilisation and androgen-secreting tumour red flags.
Reviews weight, diabetes, thyroid, prolactin/drug and family history.
Assesses BMI/BP and appropriate physical signs.
Proposes appropriate targeted investigations rather than relying on ultrasound alone.
Explains PCOS and long-term metabolic/endometrial implications.
Discusses lifestyle, cycle control and cosmetic/antiandrogen options safely.
Addresses fertility concerns and follow-up/metabolic screening.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: Is a “string of pearls” ultrasound mandatory for diagnosis?
Name two important alternative causes of hirsutism.
criticalSafetyErrors: Missing rapid virilisation suggesting tumour.
Using potentially teratogenic antiandrogen therapy without reliable contraception.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded PCOS/hirsutism scenario; patient name changed and diagnostic approach updated.

stations.title: Vaginal Discharge / PID — Focused Assessment
stations.primaryCompetency: Sensitive sexual history, examination planning and STI management
candidateInstructions: Ms Maham Riaz, 26, presents with vaginal discharge, lower abdominal pain and intermenstrual spotting.
Take a focused history and state your examination, investigations and initial management.
candidateHandout: Use a non-judgmental sexual history and offer a chaperone for intimate examination.
PID is a clinical diagnosis; delay in treatment can increase complications.
simulationScript: New sexual partner 2 months ago; condoms used inconsistently.
Mucopurulent discharge, pelvic pain and pain during intercourse. No syncope or severe unilateral pain.
Examiner findings if requested: temperature 37.8°C, lower abdominal tenderness; speculum shows mucopurulent cervical discharge; bimanual exam shows cervical motion and adnexal tenderness.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Differentials include cervicitis/STI, PID, bacterial vaginosis/candidiasis/trichomoniasis and pregnancy-related pathology.
Always check pregnancy status in reproductive-age pelvic pain.
Obtain NAAT for chlamydia/gonorrhoea and other tests based on local pathway; consider microscopy/culture where appropriate.

If PID clinically likely, start empiric treatment according to current local STI/PID protocol while tests are pending, provide analgesia, partner notification/treatment support and abstinence until treatment completed as advised.
suggestedApproach: Privacy → discharge/pain history → pregnancy/STI risk → red flags → speculum/bimanual with chaperone → tests → empiric PID treatment when indicated.

checklist.criterion: Ensures privacy, consent and non-judgmental language.
Characterises discharge: amount, colour, odour, itch/soreness.
Asks pelvic pain, dyspareunia, dysuria and abnormal bleeding.
Takes sensitive sexual/contraception/STI history.
Checks LMP and pregnancy possibility.
Screens ectopic/sepsis red flags.
Plans abdominal, speculum and bimanual examination with chaperone.
Requests pregnancy test and appropriate STI NAAT/testing.
Recognises clinical PID and treats empirically according to current protocol when indicated.
Provides partner/safer-sex advice, follow-up and safety-netting.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: What findings support PID clinically?
Why should pregnancy testing be routine in this presentation?
criticalSafetyErrors: Missing ectopic pregnancy.
Delaying treatment in clear PID while awaiting all test results.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded sexually transmitted vaginal discharge material, expanded into a PID-focused OSCE station.

stations.title: Female Infertility — Initial Assessment
stations.primaryCompetency: Couple-based infertility history and rational investigation
candidateInstructions: Mrs Sara Nadeem, 31, has been trying to conceive for 18 months without success.
Take a focused history and explain the initial assessment plan.
candidateHandout: Infertility assessment is couple-based; evaluate both partners.
Ask duration/frequency of intercourse, ovulation/menstrual history, tubal risk and male factors.
simulationScript: Married 3 years; regular unprotected intercourse 2–3 times/week for 18 months.
Cycles irregular every 40–50 days. No previous pregnancy.
Past chlamydia treated 5 years ago. No pelvic surgery.
Husband has not yet had semen analysis.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Possible ovulatory dysfunction with tubal risk; male factor must also be assessed.
Initial workup usually includes semen analysis, confirmation of ovulation/ovulatory dysfunction, pelvic assessment and tubal patency testing when indicated.
Earlier referral may be warranted with older maternal age, amenorrhoea, significant pelvic disease or known male factor.
Counsel on folic acid/preconception health and regular intercourse around fertile period without creating excessive stress.
suggestedApproach: Duration → intercourse/sexual function → menstrual/ovulatory history → pregnancy history → tubal/endometriosis risk → male assessment → targeted workup.

checklist.criterion: Clarifies duration and frequency of unprotected intercourse.
Takes menstrual/ovulatory history.
Reviews prior pregnancies/miscarriages and contraception.
Screens STI/PID, endometriosis, pelvic surgery and ectopic history.
Reviews endocrine/weight/medication and lifestyle factors.
Asks male-factor history and sexual dysfunction sensitively.
Explains that both partners require assessment.
Plans semen analysis and appropriate female investigations.
Provides preconception advice and explains referral criteria.
Addresses emotional impact and arranges continuity/follow-up.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: What is the first-line male investigation?
Name two reasons to refer earlier than the usual timeframe.
criticalSafetyErrors: Investigating only the woman.
Ignoring STI/PID or ectopic risk history.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded female infertility material; patient name changed and investigation plan modernised.

stations.title: Postpartum & Emergency Contraception Counselling
stations.primaryCompetency: Contraceptive choice, eligibility and shared decision-making
candidateInstructions: Mrs Anum Malik, 27, is 6 weeks postpartum and wants reliable contraception. She also asks what she should do if a condom breaks in future.
Counsel her on suitable ongoing contraception and emergency contraception.
candidateHandout: Establish breastfeeding status, medical eligibility, pregnancy risk and patient preference.
Long-acting reversible contraception should be discussed alongside pills, injectables and barrier methods.
simulationScript: Delivered vaginally 6 weeks ago; no postpartum complications.
Breastfeeding mixed feeds. No migraine with aura, VTE, liver disease or breast cancer. Non-smoker.
Prefers a method she does not have to remember daily, but wants to understand pills as well.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Discuss LARC: implant and intrauterine contraception, plus progestogen-only methods and combined hormonal contraception when medically eligible and timing is appropriate.
Use current medical eligibility criteria for postpartum oestrogen-containing contraception and VTE risk.
Emergency contraception options include copper IUD and oral methods; timing, breastfeeding and drug interactions matter.
Condoms provide STI protection and can be used in addition.
suggestedApproach: Postpartum/breastfeeding status → pregnancy exclusion → medical eligibility → preferences → compare effectiveness → explain EC backup → safety net.

checklist.criterion: Confirms postpartum timing, breastfeeding and return of intercourse/menses.
Checks pregnancy possibility and current contraception.
Screens key contraindications/VTE, migraine, smoking, BP, liver and breast disease.
Explains LARC options and relative effectiveness.
Discusses progestogen-only methods appropriately postpartum.
Discusses combined hormonal contraception only after medical eligibility/timing review.
Explains condoms/STI protection.
Explains emergency contraception options and need for prompt use according to current guidance.
Uses shared decision-making and checks understanding.
Provides follow-up, side-effect warning signs and method-specific safety-netting.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: Which emergency contraception method is most effective?
Why does postpartum timing matter for combined hormonal contraception?
criticalSafetyErrors: Offering oestrogen-containing contraception without postpartum/VTE risk assessment.
Failing to discuss pregnancy exclusion or STI protection where relevant.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded postpartum contraception and emergency contraception scenarios; names changed and eligibility wording updated to current-guideline use.

stations.title: Pre-Conception Counselling
candidateInstructions: Ms Zoya Ahmed, 26, plans her first pregnancy in the next few months.
Take a focused history and provide pre-conception counselling.
candidateHandout: Aim to optimise maternal health, medication safety, vaccination status and fetal risk before conception.
simulationScript: First-cousin marriage planned. BMI 29. No chronic illness known.
Takes an over-the-counter vitamin supplement. Rubella status unknown.
No previous pregnancies.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Review chronic disease, medications/teratogens, genetic/family history, consanguinity, vaccination status and infection screening according to local antenatal policy.
Recommend folic acid before conception and through early pregnancy; use higher-dose folate when clinically indicated by recognised risk factors.
Advise healthy weight, smoking/alcohol avoidance, balanced diet, exercise and medication review.
Offer genetic counselling/testing where indicated by family history or consanguinity and local programme.
suggestedApproach: Pregnancy intention → medical/medication review → family/genetic risk → infections/vaccines → folate/lifestyle → referral if high risk.

checklist.criterion: Congratulates and clarifies pregnancy timeline.
Takes medical, surgical and mental health history.
Reviews all prescribed/OTC/herbal medications.
Asks family/genetic history and consanguinity.
Reviews prior pregnancy and menstrual history.
Assesses smoking, alcohol, weight, diet and exercise.
Reviews rubella/varicella and other vaccination/infection screening needs.
Advises folic acid and explains higher-dose indications.
Offers genetic/specialist referral where appropriate.
Checks understanding and arranges follow-up/booking when pregnant.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: Who needs higher-dose folic acid?
What medication categories require review before pregnancy?
criticalSafetyErrors: Stopping essential chronic medication abruptly without specialist plan.
Missing major teratogen or severe uncontrolled chronic disease.
sourceNote: Source-derived from the uploaded pre-conception counselling scenario; patient name changed and advice framed around current local guidance.

stations.title: Booking Antenatal Visit
stations.primaryCompetency: Comprehensive first antenatal assessment and screening plan
candidateInstructions: Mrs Eman Hussain, 29, is 10 weeks pregnant with her first pregnancy and attends for booking.
Take a focused booking history and explain the initial examination and investigations.
candidateHandout: A booking visit establishes gestation, maternal risk and baseline screening.
Use local/national antenatal screening schedules.
simulationScript: LMP suggests 10+2 weeks; mild nausea, no bleeding or pain.
No medical disease; no previous surgery. First pregnancy.
Family history of diabetes in mother.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: History: dating, symptoms/red flags, medical/surgical/psychiatric, drug/allergy, obstetric/gynae, family/genetic, social/safeguarding and infection risk.
Examination: vitals including BP, BMI, general systemic assessment; obstetric exam as gestation appropriate.
Baseline tests commonly include blood group/Rh and antibody screen, CBC and infection screening per national/local policy; urine testing and additional risk-based tests.
Discuss screening for fetal aneuploidy/anomaly according to gestational age/local programme and schedule follow-up.
suggestedApproach: Confirm pregnancy/dates → identify maternal risk → baseline examination → labs/screening → health promotion → follow-up plan.

checklist.criterion: Confirms gestational age/LMP and pregnancy symptoms.
Screens pain, bleeding, severe vomiting and other red flags.
Takes full medical/surgical/drug/allergy history.
Takes obstetric/gynaecological and family/genetic history.
Assesses social, smoking/substance, domestic safety and support sensitively.
Plans BP, BMI and appropriate general/obstetric examination.
Requests core baseline blood/urine and infection-screening tests per local protocol.
Discusses Rh status/antibody screening and implications.
Discusses fetal screening/anomaly scan pathway at appropriate gestation.
Provides supplements, diet/exercise/medication safety advice and next appointment.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: What are the core booking blood tests?
Why is blood group and antibody screening important?
criticalSafetyErrors: Missing significant bleeding/pain or severe medical comorbidity.
Failing to identify Rh/antibody status or key infection screening needs.
sourceNote: Source-supported by the uploaded antenatal/preconception sections; expanded into a high-yield final-year booking station.

stations.title: Obstetric Abdominal Examination & EDD
stations.primaryCompetency: Clinical obstetric examination and gestational assessment
stations.format: Observed examination station / obstetric model or simulated patient
candidateInstructions: Mrs Alina Khan, 34 weeks pregnant, attends routine antenatal review.
Perform a focused obstetric abdominal examination on the model/simulated patient and present your findings. Calculate EDD from the supplied LMP.
candidateHandout: Respect privacy, obtain consent and offer a chaperone.
Assess fundal height, lie, presentation, position, engagement and fetal heart as appropriate.
simulationScript: LMP card: 12 January 2026.
Simulation findings: symphysis-fundal height 34 cm; longitudinal lie; cephalic presentation; back on maternal left; head 3/5 palpable abdominally; fetal heart 142/min.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Use systematic inspection, fundal height and Leopold manoeuvres.
Expected EDD by Naegele method from 12 January 2026 is approximately 19 October 2026, subject to cycle length and dating ultrasound.
Present findings succinctly and correlate size with gestational age.
suggestedApproach: Preparation/consent → inspection → fundal height → lie/presentation → position → engagement → fetal heart → summary/EDD.

checklist.criterion: Introduces self, confirms gestation, consent and chaperone/privacy.
Positions patient appropriately and exposes respectfully.
Inspects abdomen for scars, contour and fetal movements.
Measures symphysis-fundal height correctly.
Uses fundal/lateral/pelvic grips to determine lie and presentation.
Identifies fetal back/position.
Assesses engagement of presenting part appropriately.
Assesses fetal heart rate/site appropriately.
Presents findings clearly and identifies size-date concordance.
Calculates EDD correctly from supplied LMP and notes dating scan priority when available.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: What does 3/5 palpable mean?
Which is more reliable for dating: late fundal height or an early dating ultrasound?
criticalSafetyErrors: Painful or unsafe examination technique.
Failure to recognise non-cephalic presentation at term when present.
sourceNote: Source includes an EDD section; this station expands it into the core obstetric abdominal examination expected in MBBS/CPSP-style clinical assessment.

stations.title: Pre-Eclampsia — Recognition & Initial Management
stations.primaryCompetency: Hypertensive disorder assessment and maternal-fetal safety
candidateInstructions: Mrs Noor Fatima, 32 years, 34 weeks pregnant, presents with headache and visual blurring.
Take a focused history, interpret the supplied observations and explain your immediate management.
candidateHandout: Severe headache, visual symptoms, epigastric/right upper quadrant pain, severe hypertension and abnormal labs are danger signs.
simulationScript: New frontal headache and flashing lights for 4 hours; mild epigastric discomfort.
BP 168/112 mmHg repeated after rest; urine dip protein 2+.
No seizure. Fetal movements present but slightly reduced.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: This is suspected pre-eclampsia with severe features and requires urgent obstetric assessment/admission.

Immediate priorities: maternal ABC, repeat accurate BP, IV access, blood tests including CBC/platelets, renal and liver function; quantify proteinuria according to protocol; fetal assessment/CTG and ultrasound as indicated.
Treat severe hypertension promptly using an approved pregnancy-safe agent and consider magnesium sulphate for seizure prophylaxis when indicated by current protocol.
Definitive management depends on maternal/fetal condition and gestation; senior obstetric decision regarding timing of birth is essential.
suggestedApproach: Recognise severity → ABC/vitals → labs → antihypertensive → magnesium consideration → fetal assessment → senior delivery planning.

checklist.criterion: Identifies headache/visual/RUQ symptoms as severe warning features.
Confirms BP measurement/repeat and assesses other vitals.
Screens oedema, dyspnoea, reduced urine, bleeding and neurological symptoms.
Assesses fetal movements and gestational age.
Requests CBC/platelets, renal, liver and proteinuria assessment.
Recognises severe hypertension requiring urgent treatment.
Chooses pregnancy-appropriate antihypertensive strategy per protocol.
Considers magnesium sulphate for seizure prophylaxis according to severe-feature criteria/local protocol.
Arranges fetal assessment and urgent senior obstetric review.
Explains need for admission and potential delivery depending on maternal/fetal status.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: Name three severe features of pre-eclampsia.
What is the definitive treatment of pre-eclampsia?
criticalSafetyErrors: Sending home a patient with severe hypertension or neurological symptoms.
Delaying treatment of persistent severe-range BP.
sourceNote: Added high-yield obstetric emergency station for final-year MBBS and CPSP-style assessment. Exact thresholds/drug regimens must follow current institutional protocol.

stations.title: Eclampsia — Emergency Management
stations.primaryCompetency: Seizure in pregnancy: resuscitation and definitive escalation
candidateInstructions: A 35-week pregnant woman, Mrs Laiba Siddiqui, develops a generalised tonic-clonic seizure in the antenatal unit.
Demonstrate or verbalise your immediate management.
candidateHandout: Eclampsia is a time-critical obstetric emergency. Maternal resuscitation comes first.
simulationScript: Simulation: active convulsion lasting 90 seconds; BP after seizure 174/116 mmHg.
Fetal heart will be provided after maternal stabilisation if requested.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Call for help; protect from injury, left lateral position when possible, airway/oxygen/suction as required, monitoring and IV access.
Magnesium sulphate is first-line anticonvulsant for eclampsia; use the current institutional regimen and monitor for toxicity.
Treat severe hypertension promptly.
Assess for complications and labs; fetal assessment after maternal stabilisation.
Plan delivery after stabilisation with senior obstetric/anaesthetic/neonatal involvement; eclampsia alone does not mandate immediate caesarean without considering obstetric circumstances.
suggestedApproach: Call help → ABC/left lateral → magnesium → control BP → monitor/labs → fetal assessment → delivery plan.

checklist.criterion: Calls obstetric/anaesthetic emergency help immediately.
Protects airway and patient from injury; avoids putting objects in mouth.
Positions left lateral when feasible and gives oxygen/suction based on need.
Establishes monitoring and IV access.
Administers magnesium sulphate per current protocol.
Knows recurrent seizure management and magnesium toxicity monitoring.
Treats persistent severe hypertension promptly.
Requests appropriate pre-eclampsia labs and fluid/urine monitoring.
Assesses fetus after maternal stabilisation.
Plans birth with senior multidisciplinary team after stabilisation.

stations.scoringAnchor: Scoring anchor: 2 = complete/independent; 1 = partial or prompted; 0 = omitted/unsafe/incorrect. Prompted items score a maximum of 1/2.
promptQuestions: What is first-line anticonvulsant therapy for eclampsia?
What findings suggest magnesium toxicity?
criticalSafetyErrors: Using diazepam routinely instead of magnesium as first-line eclampsia therapy.
Failure to protect airway or treat severe hypertension.
sourceNote: Added high-yield obstetric emergency station. Use current approved magnesium sulphate and antihypertensive protocols.

stations.title: Labour Assessment & Partograph Interpretation
stations.primaryCompetency: Progress of labour and escalation for abnormal progress
stations.format: Unobserved/static data interpretation with examiner interaction
candidateInstructions: Mrs Hira Aslam, primigravida at 40+1 weeks, is in labour. Review the supplied partograph and state your assessment and plan.
candidateHandout: Assess maternal observations, contractions, cervical dilatation, descent, membranes/liquor and fetal heart pattern.
simulationScript: Data card: 5 cm at 14:00; 6 cm at 18:00 despite regular painful contractions; head 2/5 palpable; membranes ruptured with clear liquor; FHR 145/min; maternal vitals normal.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.

keyAnswerGuide: Recognise slow progress in active labour and reassess the “3 Ps”: power, passenger and passage.
Confirm adequate contractions, fetal position/presentation, bladder status and exclude cephalopelvic disproportion.
Escalate to senior obstetric review; management may include amniotomy/oxytocin only when appropriate and after contraindications are excluded.
Continue maternal and fetal monitoring and avoid rigid action-line treatment without clinical context/current local partograph standard.
suggestedApproach: Check maternal/fetal wellbeing → interpret progress → assess 3 Ps → senior review → safe augmentation/delivery plan if indicated.

stations.title: CTG Interpretation & Fetal Compromise
candidateInstructions: Review the CTG trace description provided and give a structured interpretation and immediate plan.
candidateHandout: Use a systematic approach: clinical context, baseline rate, variability, accelerations, decelerations and uterine activity.
Classify according to the current locally adopted CTG guideline.
simulationScript: Context: 39 weeks, oxytocin infusion in labour.
Trace card: baseline 170 bpm, variability 3 bpm for 50 minutes, recurrent late decelerations after most contractions; 6 contractions in 10 minutes.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: This tracing is concerning/pathological by common contemporary frameworks because of tachycardia, reduced variability and recurrent late decelerations, with uterine tachysystole.

Immediate actions: call senior help, stop/reduce oxytocin, left lateral position, assess maternal vitals and reversible causes, correct hypotension/dehydration as clinically indicated, avoid routine maternal oxygen if not hypoxic, consider acute tocolysis if excessive contractions persist according to protocol.
Expedite birth if abnormalities do not rapidly resolve or there is acute deterioration, using the fastest safe route.
suggestedApproach: Context → contractions → baseline → variability → decelerations → overall classification → reversible measures → expedite if unresolved.

stations.title: Primary Postpartum Haemorrhage
candidateInstructions: Mrs Maryam Tariq has heavy vaginal bleeding immediately after vaginal delivery.
Demonstrate or verbalise the first-line management of primary postpartum haemorrhage.
candidateHandout: Treat PPH as simultaneous resuscitation plus control of bleeding.
Think 4 Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.
simulationScript: Estimated blood loss rapidly increasing; uterus feels boggy.
BP 86/54 mmHg, pulse 124/min. Placenta appears delivered but completeness has not yet been confirmed.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: Call for major obstetric haemorrhage help; ABC, oxygen if clinically indicated, two large-bore IVs, bloods/crossmatch, warmed fluids/blood products and activate local massive haemorrhage protocol as needed.
Uterine massage and first-line uterotonic therapy according to protocol; empty bladder and assess retained tissue/trauma.
Tranexamic acid should be given early in clinically diagnosed PPH according to current protocol and contraindications.
Escalate rapidly to balloon tamponade, theatre, surgery/interventional radiology depending on response and resources.
suggestedApproach: Call help → ABC/IV/bloods → uterine massage/uterotonic → 4 Ts → TXA → escalate mechanical/surgical control.

stations.title: Early Pregnancy Pain & Bleeding — Suspected Ectopic Pregnancy
stations.primaryCompetency: Early-pregnancy triage, differential and emergency recognition
candidateInstructions: Mrs Saba Iqbal, 30, with 7 weeks amenorrhoea presents with lower abdominal pain and vaginal spotting.
Take a focused history, state your examination/investigations and immediate plan.
candidateHandout: Ectopic pregnancy must be considered in any reproductive-age patient with pain/bleeding and possible pregnancy.
Haemodynamic instability or peritonism requires emergency action.
simulationScript: LMP 7 weeks ago. Positive home pregnancy test.
Right-sided pelvic pain increasing over 12 hours; light spotting.
Feels dizzy on standing. Previous PID 4 years ago.
Examiner findings if requested: pulse 112/min, BP 94/60 mmHg, right lower abdominal tenderness with guarding.
examinerInstructions: Allow the candidate to proceed without coaching.
Provide examination findings, investigations or simulation data only when the candidate asks appropriately or the station card specifies them.
Award prompted checklist items no more than 1/2. Prioritise consent, dignity, privacy, safe escalation and evidence-based decision-making.
keyAnswerGuide: This is a suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise because of pain, pregnancy, shock features and guarding.
Immediate ABC resuscitation, large-bore IV access, bloods/crossmatch and urgent senior gynaecology/anaesthetic involvement.
Do not delay life-saving surgery for routine ultrasound if haemodynamically unstable.
If stable, transvaginal ultrasound plus quantitative beta-hCG and serial assessment according to pregnancy-of-unknown-location pathway.
Check Rh status and administer anti-D according to current local guideline/gestational/procedural indications.
suggestedApproach: Pregnancy status → pain/bleeding → ectopic risk → shock/peritonism → ABC → urgent gynae → ultrasound/hCG only if stable.

checklist.criterion: Confirms pregnancy/LMP and bleeding amount.

Assesses haemodynamic status urgently.
States abdominal examination and avoids unnecessary delay.
Recognises likely ruptured ectopic in unstable patient.
Starts ABC resuscitation, IV access, bloods and crossmatch.
Calls senior gynaecology/anaesthesia and prepares for urgent operative management.
Uses TVUS/beta-hCG pathway appropriately only if stable.
Checks Rh status/anti-D indication and provides clear safety-netting.
